topic: Basic requirements of a fission weapons
syllabus_extract: Basic requirements of a fission weapons. Critical mass of fissile material. Basic working principles of fission weapons
specific_objectives: 36.1.1.1 Trainee will be able to explain conventional and nuclear explosion

training_aids.remarks: Refer to the master syllabus reference list
Objective: teach the syllabus extract for this lesson

practical: Review of theoretical concepts via Q&A; No hands-on practical activity available for fission weapon internals.
intro_questions: What is the primary difference between a conventional and a nuclear explosion?
Can you list two fissile materials used in nuclear weapons?
What is the general purpose of the implosion mechanism in a fission weapon?

development.content:
Conventional vs Nuclear Explosion
Fissile Material Requirements
Critical Mass Definition
Factors Affecting Critical Mass
Basic Fission Chain Reaction

Gun-type Assembly Mechanism
Implosion-type Assembly Mechanism
Neutron Initiator Function
Reflector Role in Criticality
Safety Mechanisms in Fission Weapons

Summary of Fission Weapon Principles
Comparison of Assembly Types
Role of Plutonium-239 vs Uranium-235
Importance of Neutron Economy
Transition to Thermonuclear Weapons

summary_questions: Explain the difference between the gun-type and implosion-type assembly methods.
Why is achieving critical mass essential for a nuclear explosion?
How does a neutron initiator contribute to the fission chain reaction?
home_assignment_question: Prepare a brief note comparing the fissile material requirements for gun-type versus implosion-type fission weapons, referencing concepts from the previous lesson plan.
